question: Can a bounded three-view portfolio expose substantially more exact-target surface than the failed single-view 0.98-completeness source gate on either of two consumed new scan families?

partial_view_rules.selection: Admit a partial view only when at least one quarter of target vertices project inside, the anti-sliver and inherited depth/area rules pass, then greedily add the view with the most previously unseen depth-consistent target vertices; ties use larger short-side fraction, higher visible ratio, then earlier frame. Stop at three views or zero marginal gain.

next_decision: No pass threshold is defined. Use only the observed cumulative-coverage curves to decide whether a future, separately frozen scan family should test a three-view carrier. If either side has zero eligible partial views or marginal gain saturates immediately, stop this source family without RGB/model calls.

literature_motivation.used_principle: View planning should maximize newly visible target surface and integrate observations, rather than equating one-frame completeness with all usable evidence.

forbidden_after_freeze: change the three-view budget, quarter-coverage admission, anti-sliver or depth rules after observing portfolio curves
open RGB or run any appearance/correspondence model
set a success threshold posthoc or claim a diagnostic portfolio is confirmation
reinterpret source not evaluable as an algorithm-negative row
claim_boundary: This is a geometry/depth-only posthoc diagnostic on two consumed source-not-evaluable families. It can expose bounded multi-view observation reachability but cannot establish image matching, exact-instance binding, named entrance, ownership, access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, handoff, deployment, benefit, reliability or safety.
